races.name: 1XBET.IE IRISH RACING PARTNERSHIP Optional Claiming Race

runners_data.name: Rock Iguana
runners_data.note: Prominent-style four-year-old with Alan Casey (7) aboard for Denis Hogan, returning from 79 days off; has placed at 7f on Standard ground and handles Good, though similar-going form reads 0 wins from 7 — needs to step up.|
runners_data.comment: Rock Iguana shaped well when second two starts back and again five starts back, and has run over today's trip; drawn in stall four carrying 139 lb, he rates a strong danger, though winless in his last five starts remains the concern.

runners_data.name: Inishfallen
runners_data.note: Jack Kearney (3) takes the mount for Stephen Thorne; ran 10 days ago and has consistent placed form over 6-7f on Good, a natural hold-up horse who should find a true position at the rear with very few rivals going back.|
runners_data.comment: Ran a solid second two starts back and returns on a quick turnaround of just 10 days, with experience of today's trip and conditions working in his favour; yet to win in recent starts, but our rating has him clear of this field and that second gives him solid claims.

runners_data.name: Cladach
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's lightly-raced three-year-old off 14 days with Dylan Browne McMonagle, rated 120 — comfortably the highest-rated runner — yet only two runs on record, both Good-ground, and a hold-up style suits only if the pace is genuine.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last two starts, including ninth on his most recent outing, Cladach is hard to fancy from a low ranking on our figures; he has experience over today's trip and conditions, and 14 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Slight Of Foot
runners_data.note: Hold-up three-year-old for R P Cody, back 11 days; form reading shows two placed efforts at 7f on Standard and Soft but consistent mid-pack finishes on Good — limited similar-going exposed form of 0W from six.|
runners_data.comment: Slight Of Foot shaped with promise when fourth two starts back, and he has experience over today's trip and going, arriving here fit on just 11 days' rest — the main concern is that he's winless in his last five starts and carries a hefty 136 lb from stall 12.

runners_data.name: Spent All Me Money
runners_data.note: Adrian Sexton's four-year-old ran just six days ago wearing a hood; a genuine hold-up horse by style but redistributed to midfield given the crowded rear — the style-fit discount of 0.91 tempers confidence even though it has won twice on Good ground over 7f.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a win five starts back but has gone unplaced in every run since, making his recent form a concern; he has run over today's trip and carries 130 lb from stall 11, though our rating of 67 suggests he retains some ability.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Eagles
runners_data.note: W J Lee partners this six-year-old wearing a tongue-tie; a true hold-up operator pushed into midfield by redistribution, and despite a Good-ground win over 6f in recent form, dropping back from 5-6f trips to 7f raises a slight stamina question at this pace.|
runners_data.comment: Spirit Of Eagles brings experience over today's trip and going, and her third three starts back shows she can hit the frame, but sixth and eighth in her last two outings are harder to ignore, and a mark of 57 suggests she faces a stiff task from stall one carrying 129 lb.

runners_data.name: Snowballs
runners_data.note: McCreery's four-year-old wears a visor and is another genuine hold-up type squeezed into mid-division; form over 5-6f on Good ground shows zero wins from 13 runs in similar conditions, and the step up to 7f looks unlikely to unlock improvement.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with unplaced efforts dominating recent form, Snowballs is hard to fancy at the foot of our rankings here; he does arrive on a reasonable 14-day turnaround and has run over today's trip and going before, which counts for something.

runners_data.name: Menwirr
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's three-year-old returns from 73 days off wearing a hood with apprentice Jared Huggan (10); a hold-up horse in reality, here mapped to midfield — one run from four on similar going and a lengthy absence make this an unknown quantity.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 12 of 14 on our figures, Menwirr has been largely out of the frame in recent outings, though he does have experience over today's trip and going; 73 days off adds a fitness query.

runners_data.name: Princess Chloe
runners_data.note: Daniel Murphy's three-year-old carries a hood and apprentice Terry Casey (7); a hold-up type by nature but shifted to midfield under redistribution — placed at 7f and 6f on Good ground, so the trip and surface suit, though the style displacement limits clean finishing room.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Princess Chloe faces a stiff task ranked 11th of 14 on our figures, and a speed rating of 56 does little to inspire confidence; a second two starts back at least hints at some ability, and she has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Green Kite
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners Kevin Coleman's four-year-old, last seen 30 days ago; history of fading in the finish is flagged, and as a hold-up horse displaced to midfield under redistribution, the style-fit score of 0.90 is the lowest in the field — form peaked with a second at 7f on Soft.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Green Kite does at least bring distance experience and a recent outing 30 days ago — a second two starts back offers some encouragement — though ranked tenth of fourteen on our ratings, the 134 lb burden gives him plenty to overcome.

runners_data.name: Hexagonal
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's five-year-old (tongue-tie) ran 7 days ago and brings a recent 10f course win on Good ground; a naturally prominent horse who should sit just behind Profit Surge and whose stamina edge from winning over a longer trip could tell in the final furlong.|
runners_data.comment: Hexagonal won two starts back but has been unplaced on either side of that success, and his overall recent form is patchy. He has run over today's trip and returns on a quick turnaround, though his 134 lb burden is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Profit Surge
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, Colin Keane in the saddle for Gerard Keane; four days since last run, wears tongue-tie and blinkers, consistent placed form at 5-7f on Good — six runs on similar going yield five places and zero wins, so ability to convert from front is the key question.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent place-getter but yet to win in her last six starts, Profit Surge brings strong recent form — third last time out, and placed in each of her five most recent — with distance experience an asset; the short four-day turnaround and a middle-draw stall eight are the key questions here.

runners_data.name: Thurso
runners_data.note: Ben Coen rides Gerard O'Leary's four-year-old back from 27 days off wearing a hood; a hold-up horse whose sole recent win came over 6f on Firm, and while 7f on Good to Firm is on the stretch, he's one of the few genuine rear-of-field runners with tactical speed.|
runners_data.comment: Thurso landed a win three starts back and arrives here fit on a 27-day turnaround, with experience of today's distance and going working in his favour and our rating putting him marginally above his official mark. The worry is that he's been unplaced on his latest outing.

runners_data.name: Mo Anam Chara
runners_data.note: Ronan Whelan takes over for Mark Fahey on this three-year-old back from 81 days; won over 8f on Good and placed at 8f, so staying is not the issue — a true hold-up horse mapped to midfield by redistribution, though the longest absence in the field adds uncertainty to its readiness.|
runners_data.comment: Won last time out but returns after 81 days off, and her our rating of 66 sits below her official mark — she has run over today's trip, though her record in recent starts shows inconsistency either side of that latest victory.

races.paceDynamic: Profit Surge is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with Colin Keane in the saddle, will dictate a controlled, uncontested gallop on Good to Firm ground over 7f at Gowran Park — a track that rewards horses who can settle handy and quicken in the straight. Rock Iguana and Hexagonal are the natural prominent challengers likely to tuck in just behind, keeping the pace honest without turning it into a war. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up types — Mo Anam Chara, Spent All Me Money, Green Kite, Snowballs, Princess Chloe, Menwirr and Spirit Of Eagles all carry redistribution flags, meaning most will not get their natural position and will end up racing out of role in midfield; Thurso, Inishfallen and Cladach are the most likely of the genuinely held-up horses to find space at the rear. With one front-runner setting a sustainable tempo and the hold-up brigade crowded into mid-division, this race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently at a fair pace and sustain their effort into the closing stages — off-the-pace finishers face a structural disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Profit Surge Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Profit Surge dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and kicks clear before the field can organise.
scenarios.body: Keane uses Profit Surge's natural front-running ability to set fractions that suit his five-year-old's stamina, and with no rival willing to pressure him early the leader's five-place form over this course and trip on good ground becomes a major asset.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Close Late
scenarios.trigger: If Profit Surge sets only a fair gallop and the two prominent chasers Rock Iguana and Hexagonal pick up the gaps in the straight.
scenarios.body: Rock Iguana's consistent placed form at 7f and Hexagonal's recent course win over a longer trip suggest both have the stamina to reel in the leader on a flat finishing stretch; their ability to race in a natural position — unlike the redistributed hold-up horses — gives them a structural edge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to collapse the leaders and one of the few genuinely held-up horses — Thurso or Inishfallen — times a run perfectly.
scenarios.body: Thurso's sole recent win came over 6f on firm ground and he has the tactical speed to travel wide and challenge late; Inishfallen showed a placed effort at 6f on good going recently and could benefit if the pace genuinely lifts.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Scrambles Chaotically
scenarios.trigger: If multiple redistributed hold-up horses push forward early, disrupting the expected shape and causing Profit Surge to be pressured into a hot pace.
scenarios.body: The collapse of the front end would theoretically open the door for a deep closer, but with so many hold-up types racing out of role and crowded together in midfield, few are structurally positioned to deliver a clean run; Mo Anam Chara, who won over 8f on good ground and has course form, is the most credible beneficiary if chaos reigns.

watchPoints.text: Profit Surge sets off uncontested in front — watch whether Colin Keane asks for an early injection of pace or sits back to conserve; if the leader idles, the gap for Rock Iguana and Hexagonal at the top of the straight could be negligible.

Hexagonal drops back from 10-14f trips to 7f — watch whether he settles smoothly in the first two furlongs, as a horse who won a mile-and-a-quarter race recently may carry condition and need further time to wind up over this sharper trip.

The large cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Snowballs, Spirit Of Eagles, Spent All Me Money, Menwirr and Princess Chloe — will all be looking for midfield space early; watch for crowding on the bend entering the home straight that could cost several runners a clean passage.

Mo Anam Chara is returning from 81 days off — watch paddock condition and early behaviour in the stalls; if fresh and fit, the step back to 7f from winning form at 8f could suit, but the lengthy layoff is a genuine unknown at this level.

Green Kite's flagged tendency to fade in the finish becomes doubly relevant as a hold-up horse racing out of role in midfield — watch whether Shane Foley attempts to push forward early to counteract it, which could compromise others and alter the race's early pace shape.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Handicap

runners_data.name: Stugardia
runners_data.note: Long-absent hold-up filly (306 days off) stepping back in trip for O'Brien; all recent runs have been on soft ground over longer trips, so the Good to Firm and seven furlongs are genuine unknowns, but a finishing run from off the pace is her natural game and the pace shape suits structurally.
runners_data.comment: Stugardia is a lightly raced filly who shaped with promise when third two starts back, and with 306 days between runs she arrives unexposed and open to improvement; yet to win, but there's more to come from this one.

runners_data.name: Greydreambeliever
runners_data.note: Ran just eight days ago and has recorded a string of placed efforts at seven furlongs on good ground, making her the most course-and-distance-reliable closer in the race; McMonagle takes the ride for O'Brien and her consistent finishing profile aligns perfectly with a genuinely-run pace.
runners_data.comment: Greydreambeliever shaped with promise when second three starts back and again second five starts back, and her experience over today's trip and going underlines her claims; yet to score in recent starts, but she rates narrowly top of her eight rivals on our figures.

runners_data.name: Rion Rubette
runners_data.note: Won twice on recent form, both times at seven furlongs, and her two wins on similar ground give her solid credentials; she's a natural hold-up runner who comes here with fitness on her side after a 41-day break and should be produced late into a proper pace.
runners_data.comment: Rion Rubette has back-to-back wins in her recent starts, showing sharp form, and she has experience over today's trip and going. The main risk is the unplaced effort last time out on a 41-day absence.

runners_data.name: Thrifty Of Digby
runners_data.note: Front-runner dropping sharply in trip from ten furlongs, where she has won twice on good ground; she wears a hood and Shane Foley rides — she'll attempt to control proceedings, but stepping down to seven furlongs on a flat track in a contested duel against Rebel Wave is a significant tactical ask.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time out is the jarring note for Thrifty Of Digby, and she ranks seventh of nine on our figures; the 48-day absence does nothing to ease those concerns. She has run over today's trip and boasts back-to-back wins two and three starts back, but the recent form makes her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Rebel Wave
runners_data.note: Won at seven furlongs on good ground last time and naturally inclined to lead; McCreery's filly is three years old and lightly raced, giving her a freshness edge, and her most recent form profile — win, then placed — shows she can handle being pressed, making her the more dangerous of the two front-runners.
runners_data.comment: Rebel Wave won last time out but her two most recent starts before that yielded a second and a sixth, and she ranks eighth of nine on our figures — hard to fancy at the foot of the ratings, though distance and going experience and a 20-day turnaround give her a fair enough pitch.

runners_data.name: Hasita
runners_data.note: Placed four times in six career starts on good ground at six and seven furlongs for Murtagh, showing consistent form without winning; she is a genuine hold-up runner by nature but the crowded back of the field means she is mapped to midfield, racing slightly out of role — her real threat depends on the pace being true enough for her to reel horses back.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Hasita does bring distance experience and a rating of 86 to the table, but consecutive placed efforts have given way to a fifth last time out, making the step back into contention less than straightforward from stall 3 off 119 lb.

runners_data.name: Mallavelly
runners_data.note: Keane rides this five-year-old who has a fine record of placing on good ground over seven and eight furlongs, including a second at this trip recently; a natural closer by inclination, she's pushed toward midfield on the map because the hold-up berths are oversubscribed — her chance is real if pace is strong but she may not get the true backmarker run she needs.
runners_data.comment: Mallavelly has been knocking on the door, finishing third last time out and second two starts back, and she has run over today's trip and going before — her rating of 94 puts her right in contention. The seventh three starts back is the one blot to dismiss.

runners_data.name: Akecheta
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with a habit of running over longer trips (ten furlongs in all recent outings), now dropped back sharply to seven furlongs on Good to Firm; Hayes partners him but the distance and going combination is untested in recent form and his prominent style may not be enough to offset the trip reduction concern.
runners_data.comment: Akecheta has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 96 marks her out as a serious threat — but her recent run of five winless starts, including a seventh last time out, is the obvious concern on the way back from 67 days off.

runners_data.name: Pretty Omagh Girl
runners_data.note: Won at eight furlongs on good ground last time and is a natural prominent racer; Coen takes the ride and she holds course form at the trip, making her the most interesting of the prominent profiles — likely to track the pace comfortably and hit the front at the right moment if the duel up front does the damage.
runners_data.comment: Pretty Omagh Girl won two starts back but has been unplaced on her most recent outing, and 40 days off the track is a query; she has run over today's trip and carries 133 lb from stall two.

races.paceDynamic: Thrifty Of Digby and Rebel Wave are confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over Gowran's flat seven furlongs on Good to Firm ground, ensuring a genuine, unrelenting gallop rather than a false-pace affair. Thrifty Of Digby drops back from ten-furlong wins and brings strong gate-to-wire form on good ground, while Rebel Wave won over this trip last time and will not concede the lead without a fight, meaning the early pace will be honest and sustained. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can place at the rear — Mallavelly and Hasita are genuine closers who are likely to find themselves racing further forward than ideal given the crowd of midfield-to-hold-up profiles behind the pace. This race shape — a genuine duel up front burning off a big bunch of horses who all want to come from behind — strongly favours hold-up or late-finishing profiles with proven finishing kicks on good ground, as the contested pace risks flattening the front two and those who travel smoothly through the race before delivering a sustained finish stand most to gain.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace Aids Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Thrifty Of Digby and Rebel Wave burn each other off at a true clip, leaving the field to finish over their embers.
scenarios.body: The duel between the two leaders sets an honest tempo that stretches the field, and horses who travel economically in midfield or behind can exploit the fade in the straight; the seven-furlong Good to Firm trip rewards those with a true end-to-end gallop to aim at.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Dominates Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Rebel Wave or Thrifty Of Digby breaks best, gets an uncontested lead, and controls the tempo at their own pace.
scenarios.body: One front-runner seizes a clear advantage early while the other fails to match strides, allowing the leader to dictate and the Good to Firm surface to reward its settled rhythm; horses with early pace who press but don't overextend could finish strongly in second.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves only moderate and the closers are caught flat, allowing the prominent-to-midfield types to strike early in the straight.
scenarios.body: Pretty Omagh Girl and Akecheta, tracking just off the pace, are positioned to challenge before the closers can reel in a reduced gallop; on Good to Firm ground with a flat track the prominent profile benefits most when the tempo drops mid-race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Caught Short
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses after a brief duel and the race is run at a falsely slow overall clip, leaving hold-up horses with too much ground to make up.
scenarios.body: Horses redistributed to midfield like Mallavelly and Hasita, racing out of their natural hold-up role, struggle to find their rhythm and deliver a finishing run; the true beneficiaries in this shape are prominent types already on the heels of a modest-paced leader.

watchPoints.text: Rebel Wave and Thrifty Of Digby — watch the first furlong closely to see which establishes supremacy; if neither concedes, the ensuing duel will set an unrelenting early pace that fundamentally shapes the entire result.

Mallavelly and Hasita — both are genuine hold-up types mapped to midfield due to field congestion; if they fail to get back to their natural position, they race out of role and their finishing runs may be compromised even in a fast-run race.

Stugardia — 306 days off the track and all recent form on soft ground over longer trips; if she needs the run or fails to handle the Good to Firm, she risks being a non-factor despite the pace shape suiting her style.

Pretty Omagh Girl — if the early duel is fierce and the closers are bunched in traffic, her prominent position tracking just behind the leaders could prove the most advantageous in the straight with Ben Coen timing the challenge.

Rion Rubette — two wins at seven furlongs on good ground makes her the most form-proven closer over course and distance; watch whether Paddy Harnett (5lb claimer) places her prominently enough to benefit from the genuine pace without getting caught in traffic.

races.name: Edward Doran's Birthday Handicap

runners_data.name: Ohailbhic
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer for John James Feane who has won twice from the rear at a mile on Stabletrack; the drop to 7f good-to-firm is a minor query but sim-going figures are workable, and 16 days since last run is fresh enough — will need the pace to collapse.|
runners_data.comment: Ohailbhic won back-to-back two and three starts back but disappointed on his latest outing, and a return to form is needed here; he has run over today's trip and going before, though carrying 140 lb from stall ten adds to the challenge.

runners_data.name: Alfred Tennyson
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's 4-year-old carries a tongue-tie and races prominently, boasting an excellent sim-going record of 9/15 and four places from five tries on similar ground; Sheridan takes over in the plate and this 7f Gowran trip suits, giving him a live place chance at minimum.|
runners_data.comment: Alfred Tennyson shaped with promise when third last time out, and a second five starts back underlines his competitive profile; he has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 82 marks him out as a live threat — the risk is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Tokyo Treasure
runners_data.note: Patrick Foley's 4-year-old shows a consistent prominent style and placed at 7f good-to-firm last time; McMonagle is a significant jockey booking that elevates confidence, though the 27-day absence on a horse without a win in this company is a flag.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Tokyo Treasure did show a third three starts back, though eighth-placed finishes either side of it temper expectations; drawn in stall one and carrying 136 lb, he has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Send Harry
runners_data.note: Has finished second and fourth at 7f on good-to-firm for Evanna McCutcheon, and races prominently which suits this shape; the 7-lb claimer Dalton is a slight negative, and a career record showing no wins from 12 sim-going starts raises a durability concern late.|
runners_data.comment: Send Harry is winless in his last five starts, though a second three starts back shows he can threaten at this level; a ninth last time out and 134 lb to carry are the concerns, though he returns quickly enough on familiar ground over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Bofa Beach
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old hold-up type for Mrs Harrington who has placed three times from five starts on similar going, but the 34-day layoff and a dreadful 27th-place finish on soft suggests she needs specific conditions; the step back to 7f from longer trips is worth monitoring.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures, Bofa Beach faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's trip before and two placings from her last four runs — third last time out, and third three starts back — suggest she isn't without ability.

runners_data.name: Caitouna
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner — won over this course, trip and going last month for Paul Flynn and Colin Keane; uncontested lead is a genuine asset in this shape, though a career pattern showing inconsistency (559196) and the sim-going figures of 4/7 suggest she is not a banker from the front.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten sixth last time out and ninth two starts back, Caitouna has shown little consistency in recent starts and ranks 11th of 13 on our figures; the trainer's 1-from-22 form over the past fortnight is an additional concern, though she has experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Ballymagreehan
runners_data.note: David Marnane's 4-year-old has won twice at 8f on good, racing as a genuine hold-up type; assigned to midfield on the pace map because the field is saturated with closers, meaning this horse may not get the patient ride it needs over a trip that is probably too sharp anyway.|
runners_data.comment: Ballymagreehan has been out of the frame in four of his last five starts, finishing seventh in each of his two most recent outings, and ranked last on our figures here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a win three starts back offers a scant crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Fortuity
runners_data.note: Won at 7f good-to-firm for Mrs Harrington and has placed twice at 8f, showing real form on similar surfaces; a natural rear-of-field type reassigned toward midfield on the map given runner congestion at the back — Shane Foley's experience may help secure a more natural berth than the map implies.|
runners_data.comment: Fortuity has won once in her last five starts, with a fourth and sixth in more recent outings, and she ranks 12th of 13 on our figures — hard to fancy. She has run over today's trip and returns after 37 days, but the official rating of 66 and draw at stall 13 are simply noted facts.

runners_data.name: Reimagined
runners_data.note: Daniel McLoughlin's 3-year-old has won twice and has a pair of places from eight similar-going runs but is a hold-up type squeezed into midfield on the map by sheer weight of closers in this field; the 26-day freshener is fine but Nathan Crosse's claim is useful rather than star quality, and 7f may be shy of best.|
runners_data.comment: Reimagined returns 26 days after a fourth, and her third three starts back offers a glimmer, though she remains winless in her last five and will need to find more from stall 11 off 122 lb.

runners_data.name: Summer Snow
runners_data.note: Peter Lawlor's 6-year-old has three wins from 15 similar-going starts but recent form reads 0-9050 and no trainer runs in the 14-day window signals minimal prep; a hold-up horse at her best over trips longer than this, and the 42-day absence adds risk.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Summer Snow nonetheless rates 8 lb clear of her official mark on our figures, and 42 days off gives her every chance to strip fresh over a trip and going she has experience of; the concern is that recent form has been patchy at best.

runners_data.name: Bundle Of Interest
runners_data.note: McCreery's 4-year-old returns from 90 days off — significant for a horse who hasn't raced since a 0 last time; a visor goes on and the horse's natural hold-up style means it's been mapped to midfield, but the lengthy absence and modest recent form make this a wait-and-see.|
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back hints at better form, and Bundle Of Interest has experience over today's trip and going — our rating of 82 suggests she's capable of going close. The main risk is 90 days off the track leaving her short of peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Morehampton
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's 3-year-old has the benefit of Ben Coen in the saddle and has placed twice from 10 similar-going starts, but a form line of -40509 shows no recent spark; a true hold-up type at 7f who needs the front to collapse and even then has not been delivering.|
runners_data.comment: Morehampton has run over today's trip and going before and steps back out after 27 days, carrying 133 lb from stall five; winless in his last five starts, but he rates clear of these on our figures and is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Neo Smart
runners_data.note: Jim Bolger's 5-year-old races in a tongue-tie and is prominent in style, but all five recorded recent starts have come over trips of 8-10f — stepping back sharply to 7f is a significant trip reduction that needs explaining; Nicola Burns claims 5lb but the distance concern is real.|
runners_data.comment: A winner six starts back, Neo Smart has found things tougher since with finishes of ninth, seventh, seventh and fourth before fifth last time out, though she has run over today's trip and returns on a reasonable 22-day break carrying 131 lb from stall 3.

races.paceDynamic: Caitouna is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner 7f handicap and, with Colin Keane aboard, is likely to slot comfortably into a lead role without serious pressure from the field. Alfred Tennyson, Tokyo Treasure, Send Harry and Neo Smart will push forward to dispute prominent positions, meaning the early gallop should be honest and consistent rather than a sprint, creating a genuinely run race on good-to-firm ground. The hold-up brigade is substantial — Ballymagreehan, Fortuity, Reimagined, Bundle Of Interest and Morehampton are all natural closers, but with so many of them in the field, not all can secure their preferred rear positions and some will be shuffled further forward than ideal. This race shape — a single leader setting a sustainable but honest pace over 7f on fast ground — strongly favours horses who can race prominently or in the first half of the field and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs, rather than those dependent on a dramatic late collapse that may not materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Caitouna Controls, Prompt Runners Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Caitouna dictates a measured gallop and the pace stays honest but not brutal, allowing horses just off the lead to travel comfortably.
scenarios.body: Caitouna sets a comfortable tempo and the race unfolds in an orderly fashion, with Alfred Tennyson, Send Harry and Tokyo Treasure positioned to challenge from the two-furlong pole without having to overextend early; on good-to-firm ground this suits those with proven prominent-racing profiles at the trip. The front-running shape is dominant here because Caitouna is uncontested and horses who can race in the first three or four will spend their energy most efficiently.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Honest, Hold-Up Types Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If Caitouna quickens the early pace enough that those racing prominently weaken inside the final furlong, gifting ground to the back-markers.
scenarios.body: A genuinely run gallop over 7f on fast ground theoretically allows closers to close, but the reality is that several natural hold-up horses in this field — Fortuity, Ballymagreehan and Bundle Of Interest — have been pushed toward midfield rather than their natural rear positions, limiting how much late momentum they can generate. Morehampton and Ohailbhic, as more natural hold-up types, are better placed to capitalise if the front end does crack.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Overcrowded Prominent Battle Backfires
scenarios.trigger: If Alfred Tennyson, Tokyo Treasure and Send Harry all push forward aggressively and create a contested pace that burns out the principals.
scenarios.body: With four or five horses wanting to race prominently behind one genuine leader, a scenario where position-fighting inflates the early pace is plausible, and those who are restrained marginally — or who settle just off the heat — will be best placed in the final quarter mile. A strong pace over 7f good-to-firm can bring Summer Snow or Bundle Of Interest into play from further back, though their recent form is moderate.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Caitouna Front-to-Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely moderate and Caitouna's rivals fail to close the gap through the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Caitouna has won over this exact course and trip and Colin Keane is an elite tactician who can judge a pace precisely; if he nurses a comfortable lead and no rival produces a sustained challenge, a front-running victory is possible. This scenario is dampened by the fact that Caitouna carries a penalty-adjusted weight and faces a field with several horses who were competitive at this level recently.

watchPoints.text: Caitouna and Colin Keane — watch how quickly Keane establishes the lead from stall 6; if he gets a clean break and no rival immediately challenges, the pace could be soft enough to make front-to-finish viable and change the value calculation entirely.

Alfred Tennyson, Send Harry and Tokyo Treasure could create a minor scrimmage from the off as three prominent types fight for position behind the sole leader, potentially inflating early fractions and compromising all three in the closing stages.

Bundle Of Interest is returning from 90 days off wearing a visor for the first time — any signs of freshness or reluctance to settle in the early stages will effectively rule it out of contention in a race where it is already not in its natural position.

Neo Smart's drop from 8-10f trips to 7f for Bolger is unexplained and worth tracking in the market — significant money here would suggest a stable confidence play, while a drifting price confirms the trip reservation is valid.

Fortuity and Ballymagreehan are both Mrs Harrington-connected hold-up types whose natural late runs are compromised by the crowded rear of this field — watch early to see whether Foley on Fortuity attempts to push forward earlier than expected to compensate.

races.name: 1XBET.IE RACING LEGACY Handicap

runners_data.name: Glamazon
runners_data.note: Redistributed to the lead from a natural hold-up role; Shane Foley and Mrs Harrington form a strong handler combination, and Glamazon's sole win came over 10f on Good so the drop to 7f and front-running assignment are both against her instincts — style fit discounted accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Glamazon has experience over today's trip and returns 23 days after her last start, our ratings marking her out as the one to beat in this field. A winner five starts back, her recent outings have been below that level, but on ratings she commands respect at the head of affairs.

runners_data.name: Kingcharles
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a consistent record of fading in the finish; three runs this season all on Good ground returned double-figure positions, and six days since last run is sharp enough, but the form string offers little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, including a pair of eighths, Kingcharles has experience over today's trip and a speed rating marginally above his official mark — though his recent consistency is a concern as he lines up from stall three carrying 142 lb.

runners_data.name: Oppenheimer
runners_data.note: Tubed over 6f on Soft earlier this season then stepped up to 7f on Good for an eighth-place effort; true hold-up horse whose best possible surface is this Good-to-Firm, though the fade flag is a concern over a trip that barely suits.
runners_data.comment: Oppenheimer carries a solid 142 lb from stall one and has run over today's trip before, while our rating of 70 marks him out as a genuine threat — yet he's winless in his last five starts and that 95-day absence is the key question mark.

runners_data.name: Churchfield Lady
runners_data.note: John Harrington's filly wears a hood (hg:p) and has run exclusively on Good or Soft, finishing seventh or eighth in all three starts; another hold-up runner whose fade tendency limits confidence, though the 13-day turnaround keeps her fresh.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, with back-to-back eighths her most recent efforts, Churchfield Lady faces a stiff ask from stall eight off 141 lb — though she has run over today's trip and comes here just 13 days after her latest outing.

runners_data.name: Gilts
runners_data.note: Won over this exact 7f Good track configuration last time out and is a true hold-up horse pushed into a midfield map position — the recent win gives the most relevant evidence in the field and the trainer's sole runner adds focus; style-fit adjustment applies but the form angle is the headline.
runners_data.comment: Gilts won last time out but that victory came 56 days ago, leaving fitness a slight query; she has run over today's trip and carries 140 lb from stall 5, though her two prior finishes before that win were modest.

runners_data.name: Sayonara
runners_data.note: Adam Browne-Souza claims 7lb on a lightly weighted filly; genuinely a back-of-the-field runner whose best recent effort (third over 6f on Standard) came when getting a true pace, and the shift to 7f is untested for her.
runners_data.comment: Sayonara arrives 24 days fresh and has run over today's trip, but he's winless in his last six starts and that fourth last time out is the best he's managed recently — a third five starts back offers a hint of ability, yet the 133 lb burden makes life harder still.

runners_data.name: Ballerina Dancer
runners_data.note: 67-day absence is the most pressing question for Gordon Doyle's filly; a true hold-up runner pushed into the midfield map, she has faded in all three starts and longer absence will need to be overcome before she factors.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, with a ninth and two unplaced efforts, Ballerina Dancer arrives 67 days off the track and rates a significant 4 lb below her official mark on our figures — she has experience over today's trip, but little else to recommend her here.

runners_data.name: He's Holding Court
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie added (hg:tp) for Andrew Slattery's runner who finished fourth over 8f on Good — a step in trip at 7f may sharpen her up, but the fade flag persists and the 7-lb claiming rider Orla Tynan takes pressure off the handicapper mark.

runners_data.name: Beau Army
runners_data.note: Wears a visor (hg:v) and ran a solid third over 8f on Good within the last five starts; Chris Hayes in the saddle adds jockey class to a horse who is a genuine hold-up type mapped mid-field — best effort at 8f means the 7f may catch her a furlong short.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and finishing ninth last time out, Beau Army heads here ranked 12 of 15 on our figures, with a trainer firing at just 4% recently making it hard to fancy; she has run over today's trip and a third two starts back offers a sliver of hope.

runners_data.name: Garryowen Green
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie (hg:t) for Andrew McNamara's charge who has recorded five consecutive single-figure positions, all on Good or Soft; the fade flag and a habit of finishing ninth or tenth on turf means this is a handicapper searching for the right race.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with unplaced efforts sandwiched between two nineths and a fifth, Garryowen Green is hard to fancy at the foot of the rankings; he has run over today's trip before and returns after just 13 days, but his official mark of 41 tells its own story.

runners_data.name: Make The Tide
runners_data.note: W J Lee rides a genuine prominent-minded horse that was mapped to midfield because of the crowded pace picture; last four runs have all been mid-pack finishes on varying going, but the 37-day break and a trainer recording 2/14 in 14 days keeps interest alive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Make The Tide at least has experience over today's trip, though recent finishes of ninth and back-to-back sixths leave plenty to prove; 37 days between runs and 140 lb from stall 15 add further questions.

runners_data.name: Sunrise Angel
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery rides his own — a genuine prominent type whose best effort (second over 7f Soft) came when handy; mapped to midfield here, but Slattery knows the mare's needs and may push forward to claim a position that suits her better than the map implies.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Sunrise Angel nonetheless catches the eye on our rating of 67 — ten pounds clear of his official mark — and he has run over today's trip before, with 24 days since his last run leaving him fresh; the worry is that his recent finishes offer little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Fontaine Khaled
runners_data.note: Jessica O'Gorman claims 7lb on a filly whose sole placed effort in five runs came third over 7f on Good — the combination of trip, going and a light weight gives the most tractable profile in the race for a genuine closer.
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back shows she retains ability, and our rating of 66 suggests she's ahead of her official mark — Fontaine Khaled has run over today's trip and returns after 36 days, but the seventh last time out is the concern for a filly yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Miss Ivor
runners_data.note: 65-day absence and a form figure of nine over 9f on Good last time is a concern; a true hold-up runner mapped mid-field, but the fade tag combined with the layoff makes it hard to see her arriving from the rear with enough punch.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 11th of 15 on our figures, Miss Ivor faces a stiff task here; she hasn't threatened recently, though she has run over today's trip and comes back from a 65-day break.

runners_data.name: Ochtar Againn
runners_data.note: Worn a hood (hg:p) and ran fourth over 6f on Good within recent memory — the step back up to 7f may suit if the pace is genuine, but five consecutive failures to win and the fade label make Paddy Harnett's task difficult.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Ochtar Againn does at least bring distance experience to the table and a 27-day break could have freshened her up, but a fourth and a fifth amid four unplaced efforts make her tough to trust from stall 2 off 135 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Glamazon is the sole confirmed pace-setter and, redistributed to the front from a natural hold-up role, will dictate from the off on good-to-firm ground over 7f at Gowran — a track that tends to reward those who travel prominently through the race. With no genuine rival willing to press her, the tempo is likely to be sustainable rather than scorching, meaning the fractions will not be strong enough to set up a cavalry charge from behind. The field is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types, but the pace map understates the genuine forward intent of Make The Tide, Gilts, and Sunrise Angel — all three are true prominent or prominent-hold-up horses who are unlikely to accept a pure rear-division position and will push into midfield at minimum, adding some pressure to the pace without turning it into a true test. The tactical verdict is clear: a single uncontested front-runner on a fair surface, going at a controlled tempo, heavily favours hold-up horses who can produce a late burst — but because almost every runner in the field is a hold-up type, those with the best form on similar ground and the biggest engines matter most; the race is unlikely to set up ideally for any pure backmarker.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Glamazon Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Glamazon is allowed to dictate an honest but uncontested gallop and none of the redistributed prominent types apply enough pressure to unsettle her rhythm.
scenarios.body: Glamazon, racing in front out of her natural style, sets a metronomic tempo that keeps the field strung out and starves the closers of the strong pace they need to generate momentum; at 7f on good-to-firm, a horse in front and travelling well is hard to collar when the race lacks genuine pressure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Arrive Late
scenarios.trigger: If Make The Tide, Gilts or Sunrise Angel push forward into a prominent position early and inject enough pace to set up a true finish for the backmarkers.
scenarios.body: With genuine pressure on Glamazon from the second quarter, the tempo lifts and the 7f distance becomes more of an endurance test, allowing the best-staying hold-up types to sweep through from midfield as the leader ties up inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Free Win
scenarios.trigger: If Glamazon is uncontested to such a degree that she slows the race to a near-crawl in the first half, robbing all hold-up types of a true test.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race on good-to-firm ground compresses the field and turns the finish into a sprint from midfield, benefiting any horse with natural speed that finds a gap and quickens earlier than expected.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Jockey Tactics Scramble Pace
scenarios.trigger: If multiple riders try to improve position simultaneously in the first two furlongs, creating a bunched, contested race that burns pace and tests stamina late.
scenarios.body: A race run at uneven fractions — quick early, slower middle, quick again — rewards horses with athletic versatility and those who settle mid-division before producing a sustained run; trainers with recent course form come to the fore in a muddled finish.

watchPoints.text: Glamazon is racing entirely out of natural style at the front — if she fails to settle or jumps slowly, the entire pace map collapses and the field bunches, completely reshaping the finish.

Make The Tide and Sunrise Angel are genuine prominent types masked as midfield runners; if both push forward in the opening furlong they will compete with Glamazon for position, elevating the pace materially above what the current map projects.

Gilts is the one runner whose recent form (winner over this exact 7f-Good track) is most directly relevant to today — watch whether Jack Cleary allows her to travel up from midfield smoothly rather than being trapped wide or blocked in a slowly run race.

Fontaine Khaled's third-place finish over 7f on Good stands out as one of the few placed efforts in the field at today's exact conditions — Jessica O'Gorman's 7lb claim reduces her burden to an effective low weight in a race where the weights compress significantly.

The fade flags on Kingcharles, Oppenheimer, Churchfield Lady, Ballerina Dancer, He's Holding Court, Garryowen Green, Miss Ivor and Ochtar Againn represent the majority of the field — in a race likely to be run at a moderate tempo, horses who have habitually weakened late represent a structural risk to any late-running scenario.

races.name: Coolmore Stud Churchill Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: City of Dubai
runners_data.note: OR=120 unbeaten juvenile with the strongest class profile in the field, trained by P Twomey with Colin Keane-level jockey W J Lee; by nature a prominent racer who will find position harder to secure here with two genuine front-runners taking the early berths, so expect him to race closer to midfield than ideal and that positional compromise must be factored into his chance.
runners_data.comment: City of Dubai won last time out and has run over today's trip, but ranked last on our figures with a speed rating of 61, he has plenty to find; the 25-day turnaround at least suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Full Volume
runners_data.note: A genuine front-runner who has shown the ability to lead and win over this course and distance on Good ground, but faces a direct duel with the higher-rated Bellesque from the off; that contest will sap her energy through the middle stages and her form of 612 suggests she can be vulnerable when pressed across the race.
runners_data.comment: Full Volume shaped well last time out with a runner-up finish, and a win two starts back underlines his recent consistency over today's trip — the main concern is whether he can overcome that modest speed rating.

runners_data.name: Bellesque
runners_data.note: OR=120 Joseph Patrick O'Brien-trained filly ridden by Dylan Browne McMonagle who goes on Good to Firm and has won over a mile at this level; she is the classier of the two front-runners and McMonagle will be confident asserting control, though the weight of 126lbs versus rivals at 131lbs gives a marginal edge and she will need to handle the sustained pressure.
runners_data.comment: Bellesque arrives in decent nick after a win and a runner-up in her last two starts, and she has run over today's trip before, but a speed rating of 55 leaves her well below the principals on these figures, making her hard to fancy at second bottom of the rankings.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Rain
runners_data.note: Jim Bolger's consistent filly with five runs at the trip in similar going and a win over a mile on Good ground showing genuine stamina, but she is a natural prominent racer who finds herself mapped to the rear because the field is loaded with pace; her STYLE_FIT flag of 0.84 means she is unlikely to get her preferred racing position and that tactical dislocation is a real handicap.
runners_data.comment: Sea Of Rain comes here on the back of a win last time out and has solid placed efforts two and three starts back, with experience over today's trip and a fit 15-day turnaround working in her favour; the main query is whether our rating of 77 leaves her vulnerable to the top-rated runner.

runners_data.name: Sergei Diaghilev
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien-trained colt whose last run was a poor ninth suggests a form reversal is possible after 51 days off, but his sole win came over 6f and this step to a flat mile on Good to Firm is a question mark; as a natural prominent type with legitimate class he is well-placed to track the contested pace and his fresh status and yard form make him a significant player.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win two starts back and has going experience to call on; the 51-day absence is the one query, but at the top of the ratings and carrying 131 lb from stall six, Sergei Diaghilev looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Venetian Power
runners_data.note: Second Joseph Patrick O'Brien runner in the race, with a win at 8f on Good ground and only four furlongs of 7f form behind him; J M Sheridan takes over in the saddle and the horse carries the same yard profile as Bellesque, so stable tactics may be worth monitoring — he could slot into a prominent tracking position if Bellesque takes the lead and may benefit from any late collapse.
runners_data.comment: Venetian Power won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a clear threat from stall one; the main risk is whether he can back that up off just 23 days' rest carrying 131 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Bellesque and Full Volume are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over this flat Gowran mile on Good to Firm ground, creating an honest, pressured gallop rather than a false crawl. With two genuine pace-setters likely to push each other through the early stages, the race sets up as a true-run contest where early fractions will be honest and the premium will be on horses who can sustain their effort through the final two furlongs rather than accelerate from a standing start. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all slot into their natural positions — Bellesque and Full Volume are best-placed to actually secure early berths, while City of Dubai is the standout horse pushed back from its true prominent role and Sea Of Rain is similarly displaced toward the rear. This shape firmly favours resolute prominent-to-midfield gallopers with proven stamina at the trip on good ground — horses who can track the contested pace and hit the line hard, rather than those who need a steady pace to produce a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Lands
scenarios.trigger: If Bellesque and Full Volume fight it out up front and the race is genuinely run, allowing a quality prominent tracker to produce a sustained late surge.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other up through a true gallop, leaving the prominent horses who settled just off the pace with lengths in hand entering the straight; on Good to Firm ground over a flat mile this scenario rewards class and stamina over pure sprint speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace-setters — most likely Bellesque — dominates early and Full Volume cracks, allowing the leader to dictate and control the tempo from the front.
scenarios.body: Bellesque, trained by Joseph Patrick O'Brien and ridden by Dylan Browne McMonagle, has the class and the one-mile form to simply take over when the rival falters, building a cushion in the straight that pursuers cannot close; her OR=120 and strong sim-going record make this a credible outcome if the contested duel resolves quickly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is truly scorching and the front two tie each other up badly enough to compress the finish and allow the deepest-sitting horses to swoop.
scenarios.body: Sea Of Rain is the nominal hold-up runner here but is a displaced prominent type, so this scenario carries inherent risk; should the pace collapse the field into a heap approaching the final furlong, Sea Of Rain's course and distance form at this level gives it an outside chance to grab a placing.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: False Pace, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners settle into a tactical crawl rather than fighting it out, turning the race into a late dash.
scenarios.body: This outcome is unlikely given both Bellesque and Full Volume have strong pace profiles and neither jockey will want to gift the race, but if it materialises it would suit horses with sharp acceleration; Venetian Power, with a win at 8f on Good ground, has enough tactical speed to be dangerous in a bunched finish.

watchPoints.text: Bellesque and Full Volume are on a collision course for the lead — watch the first two furlongs closely to see which one blinks first, as the outcome of that duel effectively decides the race shape for all six runners.

City of Dubai's redistribution to midfield is the single biggest tactical distortion in this race — if W J Lee pushes him forward early against the pace bias of the map, he could still travel prominently and dramatically shorten his odds of winning; watch his early position at the first bend.

Sergei Diaghilev has been off 51 days and his last run was a listless ninth — if he shows any signs of freshness or sluggishness in the early stages after that layoff, his chance of tracking the pace effectively will be undermined before the race develops.

Sea Of Rain's true prominent style is masked by her rear-mapped position — if Colin Keane elects to push her forward early regardless of the map, she could overcook her effort in a contested race and fade in the straight rather than arrive late as the position implies.

races.name: 1XBET.IE COMMUNITY CHAMPIONS Race

runners_data.name: Benevento
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with eight runs on good ground and two wins plus four placings on similar — course experience is a clear asset, but recent form reads 004-73 and the OR of 98 may be against lesser rivals here; Donagh O'Connor takes the ride for the in-form Robson De Aguiar yard, 13 days since last run.
runners_data.comment: Benevento returns on a quick 13-day turnaround with experience of both today's trip and going, and a rating of 105 has him narrowly top-rated; third last time out gives him solid recent form. The risk is that he's winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Rahmi
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's seven-year-old travels widest from the draw as a hold-up specialist; has 12 runs on good going with two wins and five places but is almost exclusively a 7f performer and a mile tests his stamina — apprentice Rory Mulligan's claim is the main compensating factor.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Rahmi has nonetheless run over today's trip and returns on a manageable 30-day break, carrying 138 lb from stall two; our figures rate him second of seven, making him worth serious consideration on profile.

runners_data.name: God Of Power
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's lightly-raced three-year-old carries promising form including a recent 7f win and two places over 8f on good ground — three from five on similar going is encouraging; Sam Coen's 5lb claim reduces the weight burden significantly and the step back to a mile suits his profile.
runners_data.comment: God Of Power has one win in his last five starts, that success coming three starts back, and a ten-point gap between his official mark and our rating makes him hard to fancy; he has run over today's trip, at least.

runners_data.name: Anushka
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's three-year-old won on soft but has run six times on good or faster with zero wins and only two placings — she is a genuine hold-up type operating in a race where the pace map cannot accommodate all rear-runners, meaning she will likely be closer to the action than her style suits; W J Lee rides and the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.92 tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Anushka shaped with promise when third two starts back and has experience over today's trip, while her official mark of 81 leaves room to exploit on her best form — the main concern is that unplaced effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Keep It Together
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old with a record that reads 12th and 14th from his last two starts over trips far beyond today's mile — dropping back dramatically in trip looks like a significant mismatch and his 0W0P record across the last five runs on good ground confirms he is deeply out of form; the fades-in-finish flag compounds the concern.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in her last two starts, Keep It Together is lightly raced and open to plenty of improvement; drawing stall one, she carries 130 lb fresh off a 37-day break and remains unexposed enough to leave those efforts behind.

runners_data.name: Celtic Motif
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner, who won over 8f on good going and has been placed four times from six on similar conditions — tongue-tie fitted and Joseph Patrick O'Brien's dominant 14-day record (12/73) makes this a serious yard contender; uncontested pace is his biggest asset today.
runners_data.comment: Celtic Motif arrives on the back of a win last time out and has solid placed efforts threading through her recent form, while experience over today's trip and going is a clear asset; the main concern is that our rating suggests she may be a shade below the very best here.

runners_data.name: Felix Guido
runners_data.note: A prominently-raced type who won his first three starts but then blew out on his only run over 8f on good, and is now back after 102 days off — the fades-in-finish flag plus the lengthy layoff make his starting position in the market hard to trust; Dylan Browne McMonagle's booking is the one factor that keeps him in the conversation.
runners_data.comment: Felix Guido won three of his last four starts but that rich vein looks hard to trust here — he's been off 102 days, our rating puts him well below the field, and while he has run over today's trip, the weight burden of 137 lb adds another hurdle.

races.paceDynamic: Celtic Motif is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, is set to bowl along at a comfortable, self-regulated tempo on good-to-firm ground over a mile at Gowran. God Of Power and Benevento will push to sit prominently just off the pace, but neither has the gate-speed or inclination to pressure Celtic Motif into running a truly searching early gallop, meaning the fractions will be controlled rather than punishing. Felix Guido is also a prominent type but returns after 102 days off and is tagged as a horse who fades in finish, so his influence on pace shape is uncertain; Keep It Together and Rahmi will be at the rear with no influence on tempo whatsoever. This is a classic lone-leader setup where the pace is sustainable and not pressured, heavily favouring horses with the tactical speed to travel close to Celtic Motif and produce a finish — prominently-placed runners with a clean passage are the primary beneficiaries, while genuine hold-up types face a stern test of whether they can close on a well-rated leader who has not been softened up. The field holds more hold-up types than the rear of the race can realistically accommodate; Anushka, though mapped to midfield, is a true hold-up runner displaced forward on the map because the configuration lacks enough space at the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Celtic Motif Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Celtic Motif dictates a controlled tempo from the front and the prominent pair fail to close down the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: Celtic Motif, uncontested and settled in front, sets a measured pace that preserves his stamina reserves for a strong finish, making him exceptionally difficult to catch on good-to-firm ground; his trainer Joseph Patrick O'Brien has 12 winners from 73 runners in the past 14 days, underlining powerful current form. God Of Power and Benevento, tracking closest, are the horses best placed to challenge but may find Celtic Motif has simply stolen enough of a margin in the middle section to hold on.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If God Of Power or Benevento travel prominently into the straight and produce a sustained finishing effort to reel in Celtic Motif.
scenarios.body: The moderate gallop set by Celtic Motif keeps everyone covered up for longer than ideal, compressing the field into the straight and giving the prominent pair a genuine chance to sprint past; God Of Power, who won on similar going at 7f and has been placed twice over 8f on good, has the profile to pounce. Benevento has course-relevant experience and sits close enough throughout to take advantage if Celtic Motif's effort flattens.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs and hold-up types generate enough momentum to pick off tired rivals.
scenarios.body: Rahmi or Anushka would need Celtic Motif to have gone too hard early — which the data says is unlikely given no true challenger — but a compressed mid-race gallop could still leave enough late gaps if front-runners tie up; Rahmi, operating over his best 7f trip at a mile, is the least certain to get home but has six placings on good ground. Anushka is a true hold-up runner who is effectively racing out of her preferred role here and needs things to fall perfectly to make an impact.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Faders Collapse, Rank Outsider Sneaks
scenarios.trigger: If both Celtic Motif and Felix Guido fade dramatically and the race opens up for an unexpected winner.
scenarios.body: Felix Guido is tagged as a fader and returns from 102 days off; if he pushes forward and then weakens, combined with Celtic Motif blowing up, a chaotic finish could produce a surprise result. This scenario is highly unlikely given the controlled pace shape but Keep It Together, despite dire recent form, is at least qualified for staying trips and could theoretically inherit a position — though his form figures of 0-0 make this a remote outcome.

watchPoints.text: Celtic Motif jumps cleanly and bowls clear — if no horse applies pressure by halfway, watch for him to simply lengthen the lead through the home straight and never be caught.

Felix Guido returns after 102 days off and is tagged as a fader — if he pushes forward aggressively in the early stages, monitor whether he causes Celtic Motif to quicken sooner than ideal, which would compress the scenario probabilities.

Anushka is a true hold-up type displaced forward on the pace map — watch whether W J Lee attempts to drop her out to her natural position regardless, as her STYLE_FIT of 0.92 means racing in traffic or at an awkward pace will markedly reduce her effectiveness.

God Of Power's OR of 88 is the lowest among the prominent runners but his three-year-old allowance and Sam Coen's 5lb claim mean he is effectively the lightest-weighted competitive horse — if he tracks Celtic Motif closely from early, he merits close watching in the final furlong.

Keep It Together's last two runs were over 12f and 16f — the switch to 1m is so extreme that any signs of him travelling or finishing strongly should be noted, as it would represent a genuine form reversal rather than expected improvement.

races.name: 1XBET.IE COMMITMENT TO IRISH RACING (Ladies) Handicap

runners_data.name: Gatsby Grey
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced at 10 years old with just three runs in 2024 over much longer trips (22f, 26f, 23f) and no recent win in similar going; hold-up style is genuine but the trip step-down here and lengthy 105-day layoff make impact hard to envisage.
runners_data.comment: Gatsby Grey has been winless in his last three starts but shaped with promise on his two fifth-place efforts, and a 105-day break could have him freshened up nicely; our figures suggest he's better than his official mark of 72 implies.

runners_data.name: Forthill
runners_data.note: Trainer Twomey in solid 14-day form (3/10) and Forthill is the race's only true pace-setter, but its best form is over shorter on softer surfaces and it is racing out of its natural role; if it does lead, the slow tempo it creates benefits others more than itself.
runners_data.comment: Forthill has shown consistent ability in recent starts, finishing third last time out and placing on two of her last four outings, and she has run over today's trip before — the main concern is whether she can convert her proximity into something more decisive, having yet to win in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Pahlavi
runners_data.note: Strong record in similar going (14 of 15 runs on Good or faster), consistent string of placed efforts at this trip on Good ground for Hanlon, and a hold-up style that suits a prominent track from the rear of the lead group; the tp headgear suggests a switch-off job in mind.
runners_data.comment: Pahlavi arrives with strong claims on our rating, where he heads the field, and has run over today's trip and going — a second three starts back underlines his quality. Yet to win in recent starts and carrying 161 lb for a trainer in lean form are the concerns.

runners_data.name: Liberated Light
runners_data.note: Won over 16f on Good at this trip and placed again over the same trip, giving genuine course-and-distance claims; hold-up style suits the expected race shape and the t headgear is worn, though nine similar-going efforts suggests consistent but not dominant finishing.

runners_data.name: Monntie
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a tidy recent record (2nd, 3rd, 4th across last three runs) all on Good ground and all over this sort of trip; prominent style means she is one of the horses most naturally suited to the expected positional battle just off Forthill, and Hanlon sends her back quickly after 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Monntie showed grit when third last time out, and has run over today's trip, but she's winless in her last three starts and carries a hefty 154 lb — compounded by a trainer operating at just 5% in the past fortnight, she faces stiff challenges here.

runners_data.name: Numidia
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at 13f and 14f on Good earlier this season makes her a serious form contender; she is a genuine hold-up runner whose two recent wins came with a patient ride, though the map places her forward because the field is loaded with closers — her best case depends on getting a clear run late.
runners_data.comment: Numidia boasts back-to-back wins and returns fit on 21 days' rest, with experience over today's trip and going in his favour; however, he carries 154 lb and those two unplaced efforts in recent starts hint at inconsistency that makes him a each-way proposition at best.

runners_data.name: L'Un Deux Trois
runners_data.note: Veteran 10-year-old with a mediocre recent record (0W1P in 15 similar-going runs) and a 91-day break since last seen; naturally a hold-up horse pushed forward on the map, but the weight of evidence from a long career at this level suggests limited upside regardless of position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, though a second four starts back and third five starts back hint at ability; the query is whether 91 days off has left him short of peak fitness, and 153 lb is no help as he returns to familiar distance and going.

runners_data.name: Ms Messi
runners_data.note: 275-day absence is a significant concern and she fades in the finish according to form flags; her one win on Good came over 12f, which is shorter than today's 1m4½f trip, and despite being a hold-up type she is effectively racing cold off a long layoff.
runners_data.comment: A winner in her last five starts but that came four runs back, and she arrives 275 days later, carrying a hefty 148 lb with a trainer firing at just 5% recently — she has run over today's trip, though the layoff and weight make confidence hard to find.

runners_data.name: Vervain
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with placed efforts on Good ground at 12f but stepping up to 1m4½f for the first time today; t headgear worn, fades in the finish, and the trip extension is an unknown that represents the biggest question mark against her chances.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with two fourths her best efforts in recent form, Vervain is hard to fancy from a lowly mark of 53 — though she has run over today's trip and returns on a reasonable 23-day break.

runners_data.name: Mapa
runners_data.note: Returned just seven days ago and fades in the finish; recent form shows a string of double-figure finishes and zero wins or places on Good ground in 15 attempts, making it very hard to construct a winning scenario regardless of race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts with three unplaced efforts on the bounce, Mapa is hard to fancy despite returning quickly seven days ago and having run over today's trip and going before; ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, she faces a stiff task under 142 lb.

runners_data.name: Anightaway
runners_data.note: Won over 14f on Good as recently as this season, which is the most directly relevant piece of form in the race; she is a genuine stay-on hold-up type who ran back just two days ago, and while fatigue is a concern, she gets into this race off a low weight (146lbs) and that recent win is hard to ignore.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win last time out but that came just two days ago, leaving recovery time a major concern, and he sits last on our figures in an 11-runner field. Has run over today's trip, though three unplaced efforts in recent starts temper enthusiasm considerably.

races.paceDynamic: Forthill is the lone confirmed front runner in this 1m4½f handicap on Good to Firm ground at Gowran Park, and with no other genuine pace challenger likely to push from the front, she should control proceedings at a comfortable, unhurried tempo. That sole pace source sets up a race that will almost certainly be slowly-run in the early stages before quickening into the straight, placing a premium on horses positioned to travel within striking range rather than those forced to close from far back. The overwhelming majority of this field — Numidia, L'Un Deux Trois, Ms Messi, Vervain, Mapa and Anightaway — are true hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because there are far more hold-up horses than genuine closers can realistically slot in behind Forthill; of these, Numidia and Monntie are best placed to actually secure prominent ground. The race shape overwhelmingly favours a horse racing in the prominent-to-midfield zone that can travel economically off Forthill's uncontested lead and produce a sustained run from the top of the straight, making prominent-tracking profile horses the clear tactical beneficiaries here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Forthill Controls, Trackers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Forthill leads unchallenged and sets a steady gallop that suits prominent runners who travel just behind and pounce in the straight.
scenarios.body: Forthill's uncontested lead creates an economy-of-effort race where horses racing second or third on the bridle hold a decisive positional edge entering the final two furlongs; on Good to Firm Gowran ground, this suits runners with a turn of foot rather than grinders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely slow enough that the field concertinas and true hold-up runners get a clean run through in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A crawl early means the closing kick matters less than the run of the race, but genuinely well-handicapped hold-up horses with strong recent form — particularly Numidia, who has won twice at this trip on Good — could pick up through tired rivals.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Forthill Front-Runs To Victory
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is slow enough and Forthill's rivals are so disorganised positionally that she steals enough ground to hold on under a patient ride.
scenarios.body: Forthill is tagged racing out of role at this trip and surface, having form over shorter on softer, but a truly uncontested lead over 1m4½f on fast ground is a rare gift; Ms J I Stokes setting her own fractions could see her last further than expected.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rough Pace, Chaos Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If multiple hold-up horses push forward to dispute against type and create more pace than expected, scrambling positions throughout.
scenarios.body: A scrambled early order on Good to Firm over this longer trip can see pace collapse dramatically in the closing stages, handing a strong-staying, lightly-weighted hold-up horse an unlikely run to the line.

watchPoints.text: Numidia's jockey Miss N Fahey must find a clear passage from a compressed midfield pack — if traffic builds in the straight, her two wins at this distance become irrelevant.
Anightaway ran only two days ago and this rapid turnaround at 1m4½f warrants close monitoring in the paddock for any sign of fatigue before the race.

Forthill's early gallop will set the entire race tempo — watch whether Ms J I Stokes attempts to creep away or is content to dawdle, as even a two-length variation in lead margin reshapes which closers can pounce.
Monntie and Pahlavi share the same trainer (Hanlon, T14 1/17) — watch for tactical coordination between their riders that could compromise one for the benefit of the other.

The going is reported Good to Firm for this race despite the official card showing Good — horses with top-speed figures on faster ground (Pahlavi: 14/15 Good-or-faster runs) hold a subtle edge over those whose best form came on softer surfaces.
